prompt:
You are a senior typographer and information designer. You lay out data tables for publication. You judge layouts by looking at the rendered result as a whole: what the table is for, how a reader scans and compares it, which columns belong together or play the same role, proportion and rhythm across columns, a clear hierarchy of headers and groups, whether rows read as units, whether words, numbers and identifiers stay intact, and how text and white space are distributed. Fewer lines or a shorter table is not automatically better, and neither is equal widths or symmetry; decide case by case and say why.

Table: Distributed Systems Glossary (language en).
Grid: 3 columns × 8 rows. Row headers: yes (first logical column identifies each row).
Per-column content facts (content px at 13px font, excluding padding):
  col 1: header "Term" · longest unbreakable word 87px · one-line width 135px
  col 2: header "Definition" · longest unbreakable word 95px · one-line width 1303px
  col 3: header "Example" · longest unbreakable word 73px · one-line width 721px
Each column also has 21px of padding+border, so a column given width w px shows w−21 px of text.
Available width: 565px (the dashed pink box = the reader's viewport). The column widths you choose must sum to at most 564px.
Fixed: content, font, 13px font size, padding, borders, colours, alignment. You control ONLY the column widths.

The image shows the table's content with every cell on one line, so you can read everything. Study it first.
1) Understand it: what is the table for, how will people read, scan and compare it, which columns play the same or similar role, which values must stay intact, which text may wrap naturally, and where existing row height could absorb wrapping.
2) Propose 3 genuinely different column-width designs for 565px (different strategies, not small variations).
Reply ONLY JSON: {"understanding":{"purpose":"","reading":"","groups":["columns that belong together and why"],"keep_intact":[""],"may_wrap":[""]},"designs":[{"name":"A","widths":[int px per column, column 1 first],"idea":"one sentence"}]}

log.raw: {"understanding":{"purpose":"Help readers understand distributed-systems terms through definitions and examples.","reading":"Readers scan the first column for a term, then read across the row to connect its definition with an example; they may also compare definitions or examples down a column.","groups":["Definition and Example are companion prose columns: one explains the concept and the other illustrates it.","Term is the row identifier and should remain easy to scan independently."],"keep_intact":["Unbreakable technical words and identifiers","Term labels where practical"],"may_wrap":["Definitions and examples at natural word boundaries","Multiword terms when needed; their wrapping can fit within the height created by longer prose"]},"designs":[{"name":"A","widths":[156,245,163],"idea":"Keep even the longest term on one line and give definitions more space than examples."},{"name":"B","widths":[120,210,234],"idea":"Favor examples for readers who learn by illustration, accepting some wrapping in term labels and definitions."},{"name":"C","widths":[108,300,156],"idea":"Maximize definition width while allowing multiword terms and examples to wrap within the resulting row heights."}]}
